q: בת 73, מגיעה למיון עקב קוצר נשימה. היא מתארת החמרה במצבה בחודש האחרון, עם קוצר נשימה, ירידה תפקודית, וסחרחורת במאמץ מינימאלי מזה כשבוע. אושפזה בחצי שנה האחרונה 6 פעמים עקב קוצר נשימה, כאבים בחזה ובצקות פריפריות. ברקע - מחלת לב איסכמית, מחלת כלי דם היקפיים, היצרות עורק כלייתי, סוכרת. עברה ניתוח מעקפים לפני כ- 10 שנים, וצנתור אחרון במשך אשפוזה האחרון עם התערבות למעקפים ופתיחתם, כמו כן הושתל סטנט לעורק כלייתי המוצר. בבדיקה- לחץ דם 110/70, דופק 130, נשימות 24, מעבדה- BUN 23, קריאטינין 1.5 בהחמרה מבסיס. אקוקרדיוגרפיה הראתה חדר שמאל מורחב עם מקטע פליטה 20% ואי ספיקה מיטראלית קלה. איזו מההתערבויות הבאות יכולה לשפר את איכות חייה ולהאריך אותם?
o: השתלת לב
מכשיר תומך בחדר שמאל Left ventricular assisted device
הזלפת תכשירים אינוטרופיים כגון DOBUTAMINE או MILRINONE
אין מה שיכול לשפר את מצבה, יש להעבירה לטיפול פליאטיבי בלבד
explanation:
A left ventricular assist device pumps blood from the failing left ventricle into the aorta. **Evaluation for a durable LVAD** offers a potential gain in function and survival when recurrent decompensation persists despite treatment.

**A. Heart transplantation** Age together with diffuse vascular disease, diabetes and renal impairment makes candidacy unlikely here.
**B. Left ventricular assist device** This can be destination therapy for a selected patient who cannot receive a transplant. Assess frailty, organ function, bleeding and infection risk, support at home and her preferences before offering surgery.
**C. Continuous inotrope** Dobutamine or milrinone may relieve refractory symptoms or bridge to another therapy. Long-term infusion carries arrhythmic risk and lacks an established survival benefit.
**D. Palliation alone** She can receive symptom care during assessment for a device. Recurrent admissions alone do not rule out an intervention.

Reference · Hazzard 7e, p. 1202. Hazzard 8e, pp. 1189–1190.

q: בת 86, התקבלה למחלקת סיעוד מורכב עקב פצע לחץ דרגה 4 עמוק ומזוהם באזור הסאקרום. קיבלה טיפול מקומי בפצע באמצעות ניקוי והסרת הרקמות הנימקיות. כעבור שבועיים עדיין הפרשה מרובה עם ריח אופנסיבי, סימני צלוליטיס מסביב, ללא חום סיסטמי. בספירת דם 13,000 לויקוציטים, CRP = 24.5 (תקין עד 0.5). נלקח מטוש לתרבית עם צמיחה של Pseudomonas aeruginosa ו- Providencia. מה הטיפול המתאים במצב זה?
o: טיפול מקומי בפצע בלבד. אין צורך בטיפול אנטיביוטי
אנטיביוטיקה רחבת טווח
טיפול אנטיביוטי סיסטמי מותאם לרגישות החיידקים שצמחו
הטיפול ב VAC (לחץ שלילי) הוא טיפול הבחירה בפצע מזוהם
explanation:
Spreading cellulitis around a deep pressure injury indicates infection beyond the open wound. Leukocytosis, high inflammatory markers and worsening purulent drainage warrant systemic treatment even when an older patient is afebrile.

**Start broad systemic antibiotics and obtain a suitable deep specimen.** A drainage swab can grow colonizing flora as well as invasive pathogens, so use reliable culture findings to narrow the regimen.

**A. Local treatment alone.** Debridement and dressings remain important. They cannot treat cellulitis extending beyond the wound.
**B. Broad-spectrum antibiotics.** Deep pressure wounds may contain gram-positive, gram-negative and anaerobic organisms. Empiric cover is appropriate while clarifying the pathogens and extent of infection.
**C. Treat only the swab isolates.** Pseudomonas and Providencia in a surface sample may omit invasive organisms. Tissue sampling gives a better basis for targeted treatment.
**D. Negative pressure alone.** Negative pressure can help manage selected wounds after debridement. It cannot replace systemic therapy for spreading cellulitis.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 695, 697. WHS pressure ulcer guidelines, 2023 update, guideline 6.3.

q: Which paired changes in the male sexual response with aging are listed in Hazzard?
o: Higher ejaculatory volume and a shorter refractory period
Lower ejaculatory volume and a shorter refractory period
Lower ejaculatory volume and a longer refractory period
Higher ejaculatory volume and a longer refractory period
explanation:
Ejaculatory volume describes the amount of semen expelled. The refractory period is the recovery time before another sexual response is possible. **With aging, ejaculatory volume usually falls and the refractory period lengthens.**

**A. Higher volume, shorter recovery** — Both directions are reversed. Expulsion usually becomes less forceful and rearousal takes longer.
**B. Lower volume, shorter recovery** — The volume change fits, but the interval before another response generally increases.
**C. Lower volume, longer recovery** — Less semen is expelled and more time is needed before another response. These changes can occur in men who retain desire and erectile function.
**D. Higher volume, longer recovery** — The longer interval fits. Increased volume would be the opposite of the usual age-related change.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, Table 37-1, p. 549.
ref: Hazzard Ch 37 — SEXUALITY , SEXUAL FUNCTION, AND THE AGING MAN
chapterTitle: SEXUALITY , SEXUAL FUNCTION, AND THE AGING MAN

q: An 83-year-old woman with depression has a partial response and adverse effects during antidepressant treatment. After clinical reassessment, she and her clinician agree on a medication change. Which principle should guide dose selection and adjustment?
o: Select a target dose from the usual range despite troublesome adverse effects
Start at the full target dose and escalate rapidly for inadequate response
Adjust the dose to individual response, adverse effects, safety, and drug interactions
Set the effective dose from age and weight before assessing treatment response
explanation:
Antidepressant dose adjustment balances relief of symptoms against adverse effects in the individual. The dose at which another patient responds is a poor guide when the current regimen is causing problems.
**Adjust the new drug to her response and tolerability, within safe limits set by interactions and organ function.**

**A. Pursue the usual target despite adverse effects.** A conventional range informs prescribing. Troublesome adverse effects can justify changing the dose or agent before reaching a nominal target.
**B. Start at the full dose and escalate quickly.** Early adverse effects may reduce adherence before benefit can be assessed.
**C. Individual response and safety.** Review mood and function alongside adverse effects and interacting drugs at each adjustment.
**D. Predict the effective dose from age and weight.** These characteristics can help select a cautious starting dose, but follow-up determines whether it works.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1014–1015

q: A 91-year-old man with Parkinson disease, falls, and orthostatic hypotension takes amitriptyline for pain. The team has decided to remove an antidepressant with strong anticholinergic activity. Which plan accomplishes this under Beers 2023?
o: Replace amitriptyline with imipramine for continued pain management
Discontinue amitriptyline and plan an alternative pain treatment
Replace amitriptyline with clomipramine for continued pain management
Replace amitriptyline with nortriptyline for continued pain management
explanation:
Tricyclic antidepressants used for pain can still cause sedation, anticholinergic symptoms, and orthostatic hypotension. Switching among the listed tricyclics would preserve those concerns.

**Discontinue amitriptyline and plan another way to treat pain.** This removes the targeted exposure in a man already affected by falls and orthostasis.

**A. Switch to imipramine.** Imipramine also has strong anticholinergic activity and can worsen standing symptoms.
**B. Discontinue and plan alternative analgesia.** This addresses the drug risk without overlooking the pain for which it was prescribed.
**C. Switch to clomipramine.** Clomipramine retains strong anticholinergic activity and sedation.
**D. Switch to nortriptyline.** Nortriptyline is also among the strongly anticholinergic antidepressants in older adults.

Reference · 2023 AGS Beers Criteria, p. 2059.

q: A 78-year-old woman has cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma arising in a chronic heel wound. The lesion is classified as high risk. Which treatment approach does Hazzard describe for high-risk keratinocyte carcinoma?
o: Apply topical fluorouracil to the lesion as treatment of the surrounding field.
Treat the lesion with liquid nitrogen using the protocol for isolated actinic keratoses.
Apply a photosensitizing agent to the lesion and then activate it with light.
Perform Mohs micrographic surgery or surgical excision with comprehensive control of the margins.
explanation:
SCC arising in a chronic wound is a high-risk lesion. **Mohs or excision with comprehensive margin assessment** offers local control appropriate to an invasive tumor at the heel.

**A. Topical fluorouracil.** Field treatment for actinic damage or selected superficial lesions cannot assure clearance of invasive SCC.
**B. Liquid nitrogen.** Cryotherapy for actinic keratosis offers no histologic control of deep extension.
**C. Photodynamic therapy.** A light-activated superficial treatment cannot reliably define and clear the deep tumor margin.
**D. Margin-controlled excision.** Histologic assessment identifies residual tumor that needs additional removal.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1460, 1461, 1462.

q: An older woman requests an antibiotic despite the absence of a clinical indication. Which statement about treatment risks in older adults agrees with Hazzard?
o: Reduced renal function favors routine dosing because sensitivity to adverse effects is lower
Renal function and polypharmacy require attention to dose adjustment and drug interactions
Polypharmacy makes selection easier because concurrent medications reduce interaction concerns
Increasing age favors routine dosing because antibiotic adverse-effect sensitivity tends to diminish
explanation:
An unnecessary antibiotic can harm this woman through drug accumulation or interactions. If an indication arises, **review renal function and her medication list before selecting the agent and dose**.

**A. Routine dosing despite reduced renal function.** A renally eliminated antibiotic can accumulate when clearance falls, increasing toxicity risk at the usual dose.
**B. Adjust for renal function and interactions.** Estimated kidney function helps determine dose and interval. Concurrent drugs may change which antibiotic is safest.
**C. Polypharmacy simplifies selection.** More medicines create more opportunities for interactions. For example, some antibiotics increase the anticoagulant effect of warfarin.
**D. Adverse-effect sensitivity declines with age.** Older adults may be more susceptible to adverse effects, even at usual doses.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1670.
ref: Hazzard Ch 104 — INFECTION AND APPROPRIATE ANTIMICROBIAL SELECTION

q: מהו הטיפול המועדף בגיל המבוגר שמפחית UREMIC PRURITIS במטופל עם אי ספיקת כליות, המטופל בהמודיאליזה ?
o: GABAPENTIN במינון נמוך
CALCILESS ( POTASSIUM & SODIUM PHOSPHATE )
CIPRALEX (ESCITALOPRAM)
LYCLEAR CREAM (PERMETHRIN )
explanation:
Uremic pruritus can disturb sleep and cause excoriations in patients receiving hemodialysis. **Low-dose gabapentin** can reduce this itch after skin care, dialysis adequacy and other contributors have been addressed.

**A. Low-dose gabapentin** — Gabapentin has demonstrated benefit for dialysis-associated itch. Reduced renal clearance makes a low dose and review for sedation particularly important.
**B. Potassium and sodium phosphate** — Adding phosphate is not an antipruritic intervention. Phosphate control is part of the assessment, especially when phosphate is already elevated.
**C. Escitalopram** — This SSRI treats depression and anxiety. The symptom pattern here calls for treatment directed at uremic itch.
**D. Permethrin cream** — Permethrin treats scabies. A compatible infestation history or examination would be needed to choose it.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1296, Pruritus.

q: מה הגישה הנכונה לטיפול תרופתי בהפרעות בהתנהגות של דמנציה?
o: רצוי להגביל בזמן את הטיפול האנטיפסיכוטי ולהפסיק כאשר התסמינים חולפים
שילוב תרופתי עדיף על טיפול יחיד להפחתת תופעות לוואי
מינון גבוה התחלתי יכול לעזור בהרגעה מהירה של המטופל
כאשר מתחילים טיפול תרופתי, הטיפול ההתנהגותי מיותר
explanation:
Behavioral symptoms fluctuate. A psychotropic prescription should specify which behavior is being treated, what improvement would count and when the drug can be withdrawn.

**Time-limit antipsychotic treatment and attempt withdrawal when target symptoms resolve.**

**A. Time-limited therapy** Reassess benefit, adverse effects and recurrence during dose reduction.
**B. Combination treatment** Additional drugs increase interaction and adverse-effect risks and make it harder to identify what helped.
**C. High initial dose** A sedated patient may appear calmer but be less mobile or more prone to falls and delirium.
**D. Stop behavioral care** Keep environmental and caregiver strategies in place during treatment and after withdrawal.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 927, Table 60-7
chapterTitle: Behavioral Symptoms of Dementia and Psychoactive Drug Therapy

q: איזו אסטרטגיה בודדת הוכחה יעילה למניעת נפילות בקרב זקנים?
o: שימוש במכשיר שמיעה
ניתוח קטרקט
תוספת ויטמין D באנשים החיים בקהילה.
התאמת משקפיים על ידי אופטימטריסט מומחה
explanation:
Improving the visual information used to negotiate a step can prevent falls in selected patients. **Expedited cataract surgery has trial support. A spectacle intervention helped a specifically selected group of habitual multifocal wearers.**

**A. Hearing aid** — Older adults with untreated hearing loss reported fewer falls over three years after hearing-aid fitting plus audiological counseling. The effect of a device alone cannot be isolated from this combined intervention.
**B. Cataract surgery** — Expedited first-eye surgery significantly reduced the fall rate. A similar second-eye estimate was less certain.
**C. Vitamin D in the community** — Routine supplementation did not prevent falls in community-dwelling older adults, including those with low levels.
**D. Specialist fitting of glasses** — Outdoor-active habitual multifocal wearers benefited from single-lens distance glasses plus counseling. Generic prescription changes had inconsistent outcomes.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 638 and 641, with trial details on pp. 639–640. ACHIEVE secondary falls analysis, Lancet Public Health 2025, PMID 40441816.

Key note: The examination also accepts specialist spectacle fitting as stated. Hazzard limits the demonstrated spectacle benefit to a specific lens change, counseling and an outdoor-active subgroup.

q: What percentage of all hospital admissions in people 65+ are attributable to falls?
explanation:
The percentage depends on whether the denominator is emergency admissions, all admissions or people who fall while already hospitalized. **Falls account for 4% of all hospital admissions in people aged 65 or older.**

**A. 14 percent** — This is the fraction of emergency admissions in this age group attributed to falls.
**B. 27 percent** — This is the upper reported incidence of falls in acute geriatric wards, after admission.
**C. 2 percent** — This is the lower reported incidence of falls among patients in general hospitals.
**D. 4 percent** — The denominator is all hospital admissions in people aged 65 or older, as specified in the question.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 633.

q: Why can a pressure injury cause substantial deep muscle damage before skin breakdown becomes visible?
o: The overlying skin develops irreversible injury before the deeper muscle becomes damaged.
Metabolically active ischemic muscle is especially sensitive to tissue deformation.
Restoration of perfusion after prolonged pressure brings the tissue injury process to an end.
Increased local temperature reduces tissue oxygen requirements during compression.
explanation:
Muscle has high metabolic demand and lies close to bone, where compression can cause marked deformation. Ischemia makes these cells especially vulnerable before the overlying skin necessarily breaks down.

**Ischemic muscle is particularly sensitive to tissue deformation.** It can sustain irreversible damage while the skin still appears intact.

**A. Skin always injured first.** The deep muscle layer can sustain substantial damage before visible surface change.
**B. High metabolic demand and deformation.** Reduced oxygen availability and mechanical distortion work together to injure muscle cells.
**C. Reperfusion ends all injury.** Restoring flow can generate oxygen free radicals that cause further endothelial damage.
**D. Heat lowers oxygen needs.** Higher tissue temperature raises metabolic demand and can intensify hypoxic injury during compression.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 681.

q: An older adult has syncope attributed to symptomatic cardioinhibitory carotid sinus syndrome. Which treatment does Hazzard identify as the treatment of choice?
o: Midodrine as used for the vasodepressor form of the syndrome
Catheter ablation as used for intrinsic cardiac tachyarrhythmias
Carotid sinus denervation before attempting the preferred therapy
Atrioventricular sequential pacing using a dual-chamber pacemaker
explanation:
In cardioinhibitory carotid sinus syndrome, an exaggerated reflex can slow or pause the heart enough to cause syncope. **Dual-chamber atrioventricular sequential pacing** targets the documented cardioinhibitory mechanism, especially in older patients with severe recurrent unpredictable events.

**A. Midodrine** — Raising vascular tone targets a vasodepressor component. It does not directly prevent an asystolic pause.
**B. Catheter ablation for tachyarrhythmia** — This would address a rapid intrinsic rhythm. The dominant mechanism here is reflex bradycardia or asystole.
**C. Carotid sinus denervation** — Denervation has been considered in refractory cases and is not the initial device-based treatment.
**D. Dual-chamber pacing** — Maintaining rate and AV coordination can prevent the cardioinhibitory component. A coexisting fall in vascular resistance may still cause symptoms.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 675. European Society of Cardiology 2021 pacing guideline, §5.4.

q: An older adult with osteoporosis develops height loss and kyphosis without recalling severe back pain. Which interpretation is best supported?
o: The absence of severe pain makes a slowly developing vertebral fracture an unlikely explanation.
The height loss and kyphosis support suspicion of a slowly developing vertebral fracture.
The absence of neurological signs makes an osteoporotic vertebral fracture an unlikely explanation.
The absence of a recalled fall makes an osteoporotic vertebral fracture an unlikely explanation.
explanation:
Osteoporotic vertebral bodies can collapse gradually with little or no pain. **New height loss and increasing kyphosis warrant evaluation for vertebral fracture**, even when the patient cannot recall an acute painful episode.

**A. No severe pain.** Abrupt collapse can cause intense pain, whereas gradual compression may first come to attention through a change in posture.
**B. Height loss and kyphosis.** Compression reduces vertebral body height. Anterior wedging can also increase forward curvature of the thoracic spine.
**C. No neurologic signs.** Most osteoporotic compression fractures spare the neural structures, so limb strength and sensation are usually preserved.
**D. No remembered fall.** Fragile vertebrae can fracture during ordinary activity without a distinct traumatic event.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1631.

בן 80 אושפז עקב אוטם שריר הלב. ביום השלישי לאשפוזו נשמעה בהאזנה ללב אוושה חדשה – אוושה סיסטולית קצרה המתחילה עם הקול הראשון.

explanation:
A new, short systolic murmur several days after an MI suggests acute severe mitral regurgitation from papillary-muscle rupture. **Pulmonary edema** results when regurgitant blood abruptly raises pressure in a left atrium that has had no time to adapt.

**A. Marked blood pressure rise.** Forward output can fall, causing hypotension rather than a marked pressure rise.
**B. Pulmonary edema.** Abruptly increased pulmonary venous pressure explains acute breathlessness and edema.
**C. Irregular pulse.** Arrhythmia can accompany infarction but does not specifically identify the new mechanical complication.
**D. Fourth heart sound.** An S4 reflects a stiff ventricle and does not explain acute regurgitation as directly.

Reference · Harrison 22e, p. 284.
